title: DARVAZA CRATER

beats.text: A glowing pit thirty metres deep, and it shouldn't stay alive.
So what keeps this desert pit alight for decades?
And deeper down, one more surprise awaits you.
From orbit, the crater looks like a glowing hole, about seventy metres across.
It lies 260 kilometres north of Ashgabat.
In 1971, drilling punctured a gas cavern and the roof collapsed.
Engineers then set the fire to burn off poisonous gases forever.
Hundreds of natural gas fires light the floor and rim.
Next target: the most remote point on land, far from any coast. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

description: The Darvaza crater in Turkmenistan has burned since 1971 after a drilling accident collapsed a gas cavern. Its diameter is about seventy metres and the fire remains visible from space. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Source: Wikipedia.
